marta: quick question — running a mini probe on rtx-3 for seq=512. using a low sampling rate and i'm seeing big gaps in kernel entries. has anyone hit sampling bias at sub-ms sampling?
liyah: yeah, saw that on the shuffle branch last week. we switched to nsys with full capture for 15s and used torch.profiler for python ops — got the missing memcpy/kernels back.
devon: can you paste the exact command and bench config? i can spin a 20s probe now.
marta: here is what i ran:
```
nsys profile --sample=100us -o /tmp/mini_probe --capture=cuda,osrt,nvtx --duration=10s
# bench.yml: seq_len: 512, batch: 4, warmup: 5, measure: 20
```
perf-bot: scheduled mini-probe job 8112 on rtx-3 (zone-a), ETA ~5m.
sam: fyi i bumped SAMPLE_RATE to 1ms in sweep3 to cut artifact size — reduced capture by ~3x.
liyah: caution — 1ms will hide short-lived kernels (kv-warmup, small memcpy). for latency tail analysis use sample=none or >= full capture.
devon: plan: run `nsys profile --sample=none -t cuda,osrt,nvtx -o /tmp/trace_full --duration=20s` + a short torch.profiler smoke (with `record_shapes=True`). upload artifacts and i'll run flamegraph and a quick bisect.
marta: starting that now. i'll redact any S3 URLs and creds before upload. if trace >2GB i'll split into kernels/host stacks.
marta: upload complete — https://artifacts.internal/trace/2481234567/trace_full.nsys (redacted). flame cmd i used: `python tools/flame.py --input trace_full.nsys --filter 'cudaMemcpy|kernel'`
devon: grabbing it. quick tip — add `--show-all-kernels` to the flame tool to include kernel launch overhead & cudaStream ops.
liyah: :thumbsup: i'll diff against baseline-231 and post a small table (p50/p95/p99).
devon: unless we see >10% regression in median or tail, marking as regression-no for now. if anything jumps out i'll ping infra for a dedicated repro on pull-request.
marta: thanks all — will post follow-up with the compare & tiny flame snippets.
